questions.question: Describe what a complete resource list for the model tower contains and explain two checks you would make on it before the making lesson.
questions.expected_answer: Materials, each with quantity and reason: for example four rolled card tube legs 520 long because tubes are stiff, straws for horizontals and diagonals in the numbers the design needs, string for internal bracing, a double card base plate, a platform, card webs and gussets, canopy card if chosen, glue, split pins and tape. Tools with their jobs: cutting mat, craft knife, steel ruler, scissors, pencil and set square, hole punch, pegs or clips for drying joints, damp cloth. Checks: estimate the total mass from weighed samples against the 150 gram specification and reduce material on paper if over; estimate cost and note recyclable items; and check the list against the constraints, only the materials provided and no sharp parts, recording any substitution needed.

questions.question: Explain how to produce the 2D working drawing of one face of the tower at 1 to 2, including the dimensions a maker needs.
questions.expected_answer: Write the scale, then draw feint construction lines: a centre line, a base line 150 real drawn 75, a platform line 60 real drawn 30, legs joining them symmetrically, horizontal levels ticked up the centre line closer together near the base, horizontals at each level, X diagonals in the lower panels and single alternating diagonals above, the platform frame and the base plate. Darken outlines, leave construction feint and draw the hidden internal string dashed. Dimension in real millimetres, each once, outside the drawing: overall height 520, base width 150, platform width 60, each level from the base, leg tube diameter, base plate size, with a note that horizontals are cut to fit or their lengths given per level.

questions.question: What is a parts schedule, how is it linked to the drawing, and how can the drawing be used during making?
questions.expected_answer: A parts schedule is a table beside the drawing listing each part with its quantity, material and size, for example leg 4 card tube 520 by 12, horizontal level 2, 4 straws 132, base plate 1 double card 150 by 150, webs 16, gussets 24, string 2 metres. Each part is lettered on the drawing and the same letter appears in the schedule so the maker can match them. During making, the drawing, covered with plastic, is used as a jig: faces are assembled flat on top of it so every face comes out identical, and the outline sequence of manufacture is read alongside it.
